Appreciate the matrix. High level answers from our side:

- Evidence: We need a timestamped log that shows (a) tombstone created, (b) tombstone replicated to secondary region, and (c) expunge completed (or reason it did not run). A signed attestation from your security/compliance team is also useful for contracts.
- KMS destruction: In our policy, key destruction alone does not count as evidence of data erasure. We expect the provider to still show an expunge step or a documented inability to recover encrypted blobs.

Danielle / Ben —

Thanks for the quick reply, Danielle. Below is how Redwood's backup/DR pipeline behaves for the US region pairs (concise):

- Snapshot and Tombstone creation: When a delete request is processed (and not blocked by legal hold), the primary cluster creates a tombstone marker for the affected snapshot(s). That marker is a metadata object (not the blob) and is written to the primary region log with an event id and timestamp.

- Asynchronous replication: Tombstone metadata is streamed to configured replica regions via our replication queue; delivery is best-effort/ordered but asynchronous. We record "tombstone-replicated" events per-region with the original event id so you can correlate.

- Expunge epoch: Physical expunge (remove encrypted blobs / free storage) is coordinated by a periodic expunge job that moves through retention epochs. The job checks: tombstone present, no legal hold, KMS key status. Expunge is not immediate by default — it runs according to the retention configuration (e.g., 72-hour window after tombstone for this customer unless overridden by hold).

- KMS key destruction: If a customer-managed KMS key is destroyed, we mark the blobs as irrecoverable but we still record an expunge event when the background job runs and actually clears references and updates the audit chain. KMS destruction alone is not logged as "expunge complete" because physical removal may still be pending on replicas.

- Evidence we can provide: per-region event logs (JSONL) with event ids for tombstone-created, tombstone-replicated, expunge-scheduled, expunge-completed. We can also include the storage object IDs and the associated timestamps.

I've attached a short excerpt from the audit log format (audit_log_excerpt.txt) showing the event fields you'll see. If Greenbank requires signed attestation, we can produce a formal PDF signed by our compliance lead — tell us the exact clauses you need.

Naomi Feldman
Sr. Product Manager, Data Platform — Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Clarify: tombstone/expunge propagation for cross-region backup pairs (details & examples)

Ben / Naomi / Danielle —

Quick answers + examples from the infra side:

- Max replication lag: Typical tombstone-replication latency between US region pairs is 3–20 minutes under normal load. In pathological backpressure scenarios it can stretch to ~2 hours; we can include a contractual max of 2 hours for replication-delivery of tombstone metadata and provide monitoring alerts if we exceed that. The replication event includes the original event_id so you can correlate.

- Legal hold visibility: We have an explicit hold object that attaches to snapshot IDs. When a hold is applied we emit a "hold-applied" event with fields hold_id, applied_by, applied_at, reason. The expunge job queries active holds before removing blobs and emits "expunge-deferred" if a hold exists. Sample JSONL lines (excerpt):

{
  "event_id": "evt-20260601-7f3b",
  "type": "tombstone-created",
  "snapshot_id": "snap-09ab",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "timestamp": "2026-06-01T10:55:12Z"
}

{
  "event_id": "evt-20260601-7f3b-replica-us-east-1",
  "type": "tombstone-replicated",
  "snapshot_id": "snap-09ab",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "timestamp": "2026-06-01T11:00:05Z"
}

{
  "event_id": "evt-20260601-hold-12",
  "type": "hold-applied",
  "hold_id": "hld-12",
  "snapshot_id": "snap-09ab",
  "applied_by": "greenbank:d.price",
  "timestamp": "2026-06-01T11:10:00Z"
}

{
  "event_id": "evt-20260603-expunge-55",
  "type": "expunge-deferred",
  "snapshot_id": "snap-09ab",
  "reason": "active_hold:hld-12",
  "timestamp": "2026-06-03T03:00:00Z"
}

- KMS note: If a customer-managed KMS key is scheduled for destruction we mark blobs as "kms-schedule-destroy" and include the key_id and scheduled_at in the event. The expunge still respects holds and replication state. After key destruction, we can show an "irrecoverable" flag in the audit entry, but we only mark "expunge-completed" once the background job has removed object references in all configured replica regions.

- Deliverables: We can produce per-customer JSONL event bundles for requested windows, and a signed attestation PDF. I filed SUP-4729 for a repeatable request path (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4729) and added a runbook with the required fields to the Drive folder.

Happy to join a call with Greenbank Legal to sign off on wording.
